svg.title: Seven-lug terminal strip — lug assignments in the ST-70
svg.desc: A small phenolic terminal strip with seven electrically-isolated lugs sticking out. Each lug serves a specific purpose in the ST-70's grounding architecture.
svg.text: Seven-lug terminal strip — physical anchor for the ground network
Hover any lug for what lands there. Lug assignments per the ST-70's standard wiring.

g.data-tooltip:
Lug 1 — flexible / channel-specific.
Different ST-70 schematic revisions assign this lug differently. Commonly used as a tie point for the input stage's grid return, or for a coupling-cap return path. Refer to the Version B schematic for your specific board.
Lug 2 — also version-dependent. Often the bias network return point or the bias-pot reference.
Lug 3 — also version-dependent. Sometimes an input stage cathode tie, sometimes unused.

Lug 4 — central position, often used as the main signal-ground tie point — where the audio circuit's signal ground attaches to the chassis via a star-ground link (often through a small resistor or a single low-impedance wire).

LUG 5 — Heater #1 center tap.
The GRN/YEL center-tap lead from the PA-060's 6.3V heater winding #1 lands here in build step 6. This anchors the heater AC midpoint at 0V (signal ground), cancelling 60Hz hum coupling into the audio path.
See the heater circuits theory chapter for why this matters.
Lug 6 — flexible. In some configurations this is the second heater's CT (depending on schematic revision), in others it's a separate ground reference for the input stage of one channel.

LUG 7 — Heater #2 center tap.
The BRN/YEL center-tap lead from the PA-060's 6.3V heater winding #2 lands here in build step 6. Same role as lug 5 but for the OTHER channel — channel-separated heater CT grounds give better hum decorrelation between the two channels.

g.text: A small phenolic (insulating) board with seven brass lugs sticking out. Each lug is electrically isolated from the others and from the chassis.
It's a mechanical anchor — a place where multiple wires can meet at one node without floating.
Lugs 5 and 7 are the canonical heater-CT anchor points (wired in step 6); other lugs vary by schematic revision.
By concentrating all ground-related wiring here, the amp's grounding architecture is systematic and inspectable.
All paths converge at one visible location — easy to audit, easy to modify, easy to troubleshoot if hum appears later.
See the grounding theory chapter for the star-ground architecture this strip enables.

svg.text: Seven lugs, two chassis bolts. The mounting bolts hold the strip to the chassis but don't electrically connect the lugs to the chassis.
